body.mix:
Direct narration-এর Reporting verb যদি Present বা Future Tense হয় তাহলে Reported speech-এ Tense-এর পরিবর্তন হয় না।
Direct: He says, 'I am ill.'
Indirect: He says that he is ill.
Direct: Rana will say, 'I am sorry.'
Indirect: Rana will say that he is sorry.
কিন্তু Reporting verb যদি Past tense-এর হয় তাহলে নিম্নোক্ত নিয়মে Reported speech-এর tense পরিবর্তিত হবে:
Direct-এ এই Tense থাকলে → Indirect-এ এই Tense হবে
1. Present Indefinite Tense → Past Indefinite Tense
2. Present Continuous Tense → Past Continuous Tense
3. Present Perfect Tense → Past Perfect Tense
4. Present Perfect Continuous Tense → Past Perfect Continuous Tense
5. Past Indefinite Tense → Past Perfect Tense
6. Past Continuous Tense → Past Perfect Continuous Tense
বি.দ্র. Reported Speech এ Past Perfect বা Past Perfect Continuous থাকলে তাদের কোনো পরিবর্তন হয় না। Can থাকলে পরিবর্তিত হয়ে could; shall, will থাকলে should, would এবং may থাকলে might হয়। Must সাধারণত 'had to'-তে রূপান্তরিত হয়। তবে চিরকালীন বাধ্যবাধকতা বুঝাতে must-এর কোনো পরিবর্তন হয় না।
body.en:
If the Reporting verb of the Direct narration is in the Present or Future Tense, then the Tense of the Reported speech does not change.
Direct: He says, 'I am ill.'
Indirect: He says that he is ill.
Direct: Rana will say, 'I am sorry.'
Indirect: Rana will say that he is sorry.
But if the Reporting verb is in the Past tense, then the tense of the Reported speech will change according to the following rules:
If this Tense is in the Direct → this Tense will be in the Indirect
1. Present Indefinite Tense → Past Indefinite Tense
2. Present Continuous Tense → Past Continuous Tense
3. Present Perfect Tense → Past Perfect Tense
4. Present Perfect Continuous Tense → Past Perfect Continuous Tense
5. Past Indefinite Tense → Past Perfect Tense
6. Past Continuous Tense → Past Perfect Continuous Tense
Note: If the Reported Speech has Past Perfect or Past Perfect Continuous, they do not change at all. 'Can' changes into 'could'; 'shall, will' become 'should, would' and 'may' becomes 'might'. 'Must' generally changes into 'had to'. But to express a permanent obligation, 'must' does not change at all.

কিছু কিছু words/phrases আছে যেগুলো Direct থেকে Indirect করার পর পরিবর্তিত হয়। সেগুলোর একটি তালিকা দেয়া হলো:
Direct-এ এই শব্দগুচ্ছ থাকলে → Indirect-এ এই শব্দগুচ্ছ হয়
This — এটি/এটা/এই → that — ওটি/ওটা/ঐ
These — এগুলো → those — ওগুলো
Now — এখন → then — তখন
Here — এখানে → there — সেখানে
Ago — আগে → before — আগে
Hence — এখান থেকে → thence — সেখান থেকে
Hither — এদিকে → thither — সেদিকে
Thus — এভাবে → so — তাই
Come — আসা → go — যাওয়া
Today — আজ → that day — ঐ দিন
The same day — একই দিন → the following day/the next day — পরের দিন
Tomorrow — আগামী কাল → the next day — পরের দিন
Yesterday — গতকাল → the day before/the previous day — আগের দিন
Tonight — আজ রাতে → that night — ঐ রাতে
Last night — গত রাতে → the night before/the previous night — আগের রাতে
Next week — পরবর্তী সপ্তাহে → the following week
Last week — গত সপ্তাহে → the previous week
Yesterday morning → the previous morning
Tomorrow morning → the next morning
বি.দ্র. It-এর কোনো পরিবর্তন হয় না। সেই সাথে ডান দিকের শব্দগুচ্ছ যদি Direct Narration-এ আসে তাহলে সেগুলোও পরিবর্তিত হবে না। যেমন— come থাকলে go হবে কিন্তু go থাকলে go-ই হবে, come হবে না।
body.en:
There are some words/phrases which change after changing from Direct to Indirect. A list of them is given below:
If this word/phrase is in the Direct → this word/phrase will be in the Indirect
This — this → that — that
These — these → those — those
Now — now → then — then
Here — here → there — there
Ago — ago → before — before
Hence — from here → thence — from there
Hither — to this side → thither — to that side
Thus — in this way → so — so
Come — to come → go — to go
Today — today → that day — that day
The same day — the same day → the following day/the next day — the next day
Tomorrow — tomorrow → the next day — the next day
Yesterday — yesterday → the day before/the previous day — the previous day
Tonight — tonight → that night — that night
Last night — last night → the night before/the previous night — the previous night
Next week — next week → the following week
Last week — last week → the previous week
Yesterday morning → the previous morning
Tomorrow morning → the next morning
Note: 'It' does not change at all. Likewise, if the word/phrases of the right side come in the Direct Narration, they too will not change. For example — if there is 'come' it will become 'go', but if there is 'go' it will remain 'go'; it will not become 'come'.

Reporting Verb say-এর পরিবর্তে tell বসে। তবে object না থাকলে say বহাল থাকে। Comma ও inverted comma উঠে গিয়ে that বসে। Tense ও person যথানিয়মে পরিবর্তিত হবে।
বি.দ্র. Reported speech-এর বাক্যটি যদি চিরন্তন সত্য (universal truth) হয় তাহলে তার পরিবর্তন হয় না।
body.en:
Instead of the Reporting Verb 'say', 'tell' sits. But if there is no object, 'say' remains. The comma and inverted comma go away and 'that' sits. Tense and person will change according to the rules.
Note: If the sentence of the Reported speech is a universal truth, then it does not change.

body.en: Instead of the Reporting verb 'say', 'ask/enquire of' sits. If there is no Wh-question word in the interrogative sentence, then the comma goes away and 'if' or 'whether' sits. If there is a Wh-question word, it remains unchanged. And after making it indirect, the sentence becomes Assertive.

body.mix: Reported Speech-এর অর্থ ও ভাব অনুযায়ী say-এর পরিবর্তে order, command, request, advise, beg, ask, tell ইত্যাদি বসে। হ্যাঁ-বোধক বাক্যের ক্ষেত্রে Comma ও Inverted comma উঠে to বসে এবং না-বোধক বাক্যের ক্ষেত্রে not to বসে। বাক্যে please থাকলে উঠে যায় বা তার পরিবর্তে kindly এবং sir এর পরিবর্তে respectfully ব্যবহৃত হয়।
body.en: According to the meaning and sense of the Reported Speech, instead of 'say', 'order, command, request, advise, beg, ask, tell' etc. sit. In the case of an affirmative sentence, the Comma and Inverted comma go away and 'to' sits, and in the case of a negative sentence 'not to' sits. If there is 'please' in the sentence, it goes away, or instead of it 'kindly' is used, and instead of 'sir', 'respectfully' is used.

heading.mix: 21.5 (b) Let দ্বারা imperative sentence শুরু হলে
heading.en: 21.5 (b) When an imperative sentence begins with Let
heading.bn: 21.5 (b) Let দ্বারা imperative sentence শুরু হলে

body.mix:
Let দ্বারা imperative sentence শুরু হলে এবং তা দ্বারা প্রস্তাব বোঝালে Say-এর পরিবর্তে propose বা suggest হয়, comma উঠে that বসে let উঠে subject-এর পর should বসে বাক্যটি Assertive হয়ে যায়।
Direct: Rana said to me, 'Let us go home.'
Indirect: Rana proposed to me that we should go home.
body.en:
If an imperative sentence begins with 'Let' and it expresses a proposal, then instead of 'Say', 'propose' or 'suggest' is used, the comma goes away and 'that' sits, 'let' goes away and 'should' sits after the subject, and the sentence becomes Assertive.
Direct: Rana said to me, 'Let us go home.'
Indirect: Rana proposed to me that we should go home.
body.bn:
Let দ্বারা imperative sentence শুরু হলে এবং তা দ্বারা প্রস্তাব বোঝালে Say-এর পরিবর্তে propose বা suggest হয়, comma উঠে that বসে let উঠে subject-এর পর should বসে বাক্যটি Assertive হয়ে যায়।
Direct: Rana said to me, 'Let us go home.'
Indirect: Rana proposed to me that we should go home.

body.mix: Let দ্বারা প্রস্তাব না বোঝালে Let-এর পরিবর্তে might বা might be allowed to বসে।
body.en: If 'Let' does not express a proposal, then instead of 'Let', 'might' or 'might be allowed to' sits.
body.bn: Let দ্বারা প্রস্তাব না বোঝালে Let-এর পরিবর্তে might বা might be allowed to বসে।

body.mix: Reported speech-এর অর্থ ও ভাব অনুযায়ী say-এর পরিবর্তে wish বা pray, comma উঠিয়ে that এবং subject-এর পর might বসিয়ে বাক্যটিকে Assertive করতে হয়।
body.en: According to the meaning and sense of the Reported speech, instead of 'say', 'wish' or 'pray' is used, the comma is removed and 'that' is put, and 'might' is put after the subject to make the sentence Assertive.

heading.en: 21.6 (b) When the sentence has good morning/evening

body.mix:
বাক্যে good morning/evening থাকলে say-এর পরিবর্তে wish এবং good-bye/good night থাকলে say-এর পরিবর্তে bid বসে। উল্লেখ্য, bid-এর past form হচ্ছে bade,
Direct: Raju said, 'Good morning, my friends.'
Indirect: Raju wished his friends good morning or Raju wished good morning to his friends.
body.en:
If the sentence has 'good morning/evening', then instead of 'say', 'wish' sits, and if it has 'good-bye/good night', then instead of 'say', 'bid' sits. Note that the past form of 'bid' is 'bade'.
Direct: Raju said, 'Good morning, my friends.'
Indirect: Raju wished his friends good morning or Raju wished good morning to his friends.
body.bn:
বাক্যে good morning/evening থাকলে say-এর পরিবর্তে wish এবং good-bye/good night থাকলে say-এর পরিবর্তে bid বসে। উল্লেখ্য, bid-এর past form হচ্ছে bade,
Direct: Raju said, 'Good morning, my friends.'
Indirect: Raju wished his friends good morning or Raju wished good morning to his friends.

body.mix:
Exclamatory sentence-এ আনন্দ বোঝালে Say-এর পরিবর্তে exclaim in বা with joy/delight/wonder; cry out in joy ইত্যাদি বসে; আর দুঃখ বোঝালে exclaim with sorrow/grief ইত্যাদি বসে। কমা উঠিয়ে that বসে এবং alas, ah, hurrah, ইত্যাদি থাকলে তা বাদ দিয়ে বাক্যটিকে Assertive করতে হয়। What বা how দিয়ে বাক্য শুরু হলে এদের পরিবর্তে noun-এর পূর্বে great এবং adjective-এর পূর্বে very বসে।
Direct: He said, 'Hurrah! We have won the game.'
Indirect: He exclaimed with joy that they had won the game.
Direct: He said, 'Alas! I am undone.'

body.en:
If an Exclamatory sentence expresses joy, then instead of 'Say', 'exclaim in' or 'with joy/delight/wonder; cry out in joy' etc. sit; and if it expresses sorrow, 'exclaim with sorrow/grief' etc. sit. The comma is removed and 'that' sits, and if there are 'alas, ah, hurrah' etc., they are dropped and the sentence is made Assertive. If the sentence begins with 'What' or 'how', then instead of them 'great' sits before a noun and 'very' sits before an adjective.

Indirect: He exclaimed with joy that they had won the game.

body.bn:
